transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We've got about 55 minutes on the calendar, want to run through your pipeline, prioritize the top co-sell motions, and align on next steps. Jordan, want to kick us off on where you see the highest momentum right now?

[00:18] Jordan Kim (Lumina): Yeah sure, thanks Alex. Um, hey team. So biggest ones are Acme (they're pushing to production Q2), Meridian Systems (longer sales cycle, interested in Private deployment), and then a couple mid-market deals — NovaHealth and Boxwell. I'll send the spreadsheet after this but top three that we think make sense to co-sell are Acme, Meridian, NovaHealth.

[00:40] Priya Desai (Lumina BD): One note, Acme is very latency-sensitive and they asked for SLOs, also they asked about SOC 2 and KMS integrations.

[00:51] Alex Rivera: Right, totally. Samir can you weigh in on Acme from a technical/ops perspective? What does Redwood recommend — Hosted, Dedicated, or Private?

[01:04] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Sure. So for Acme, given latency and data residency plus their volume estimates, my recommendation is Redwood Dedicated initially — reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput. We can do a hybrid: start with Hosted for dev, then Dedicated for production. For Meridian, if they require VPC or on-prem we can map to Redwood Private. Quick caveat, when folks say KV cache they sometimes mean K-V cash in the transcript.

[01:29] Jordan Kim: (laughs) yeah the last call had the K-V cash comment.

[01:33] Samir: Right — our prefix/KV cache will help with token cost, but for Acme their sequence lengths are variable so we'll need to test batching profiles. We'll put together suggested quantization profiles too.

[01:47] Ethan Wu (Lumina Solutions Architect): On the security ask — they need SAML SSO, KMS/HSM integration for key management, and audit logs retained for 12 months. Do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO stuff we can share?

[02:02] Maya Chen (Redwood CSM): Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO-27001, and a security whitepaper. I'll attach the security pack. There's also an audit logs export feature in the Console; we can provide retention configuration and an account-level export.

[02:20] Priya: Great. For pricing, Acme wants committed pricing for Dedicated. We're proposing a co-sell split 60/40 Lumina/Redwood but we want your input on discounts for a 12-month commit.

[02:33] Alex: We can do structured committed capacity discounts; I'll share pricing bands. The split you propose sounds reasonable as a starting point — we'll need to map the SKU and committed throughput to an ARR number.

[02:47] Jordan: Another higher-priority item is enabling Lumina reps to demo Redwood quickly. We need a playbook and a joint deck. Also, can we get a sandbox account or quick demo flow that doesn't require security DB creds?

[03:01] Samir: Yes, we can provision a partner sandbox cluster with limited data and sample models. We'll provide a step-by-step demo playbook (screens, API examples, and a benchmark sheet). The benchmark sheet will include tokens/sec, 95th pct latency and cost per 1M tokens.

[03:18] Alex: Perfect. Let's walk the pipeline quickly — Jordan, can you call out the deal states?

[03:24] Jordan: Acme is late-stage — RFP in, exec sponsor engaged, decision maker is head of platform. Meridian is evaluation — they want on-prem options and we have an intro scheduled with their infra lead next week. NovaHealth is earlier, need to prove compliance and do a short POC. Boxwell is mostly price pushback.

[03:44] Priya: For Boxwell, their main objection is cost vs self-hosting on GCP. They call out inference unit economics and also want guarantees on uptime.

[03:54] Samir: On cost, Redwood Optimize will help — intelligent batching and caching reduce no. of tokens sent and model quantization suggestions reduce GPU cost per token. For uptime, Dedicated has SLA options; we can include an uptime SLA tier in the quote.

[04:11] Hannah Lee (Lumina Sales): For the Acme RFP they asked about response time at 95th pct for 512 tokens. Do you have numbers?

[04:18] Samir: We have benchmark numbers for similar customers: on Dedicated with A100 equivalent, 95th pct latency for a 512-token call is about 180-220ms depending on model variant and batching. On Hosted small-profile latency might be 300-450ms. We'll put exact numbers for Acme after we run the joint benchmark.

[04:41] Jordan: Are there any red flags from legal/compliance perspective when we push a Demo environment?

[04:46] Alex: We should avoid customer PII in the sandbox. We'll provide sanitized sample data and a documented data handling policy. Legal usually asks for a DPA and a security questionnaire — we can help fill your customer's vendor security form.

[04:59] Ethan: For Meridian, they mentioned needing an air-gapped deployment option. How realistic is that for Redwood Private?

[05:07] Samir: We do offer on-prem packages for air-gapped customers. It requires more lead time (typically 8-12 weeks) and an on-site infra checklist. We'll need Meridian infra details: number of GPUs, network topology, and KMS approach.

[05:21] Jordan: Okay — we can prioritize Acme as the anchor and Meridian as second. NovaHealth to follow after we show compliance docs. Boxwell we'll handle as a price negotiation.

[05:30] Priya: One ask — can Redwood provide a simple win/loss playbook showing objection handling for the top three scenarios: latency, price, compliance? That will help our reps.

[05:40] Maya: Absolutely, we have an objection playbook template; we'll customize it for Lumina. We'll include talk tracks, benchmark snippets, and sample contract language for committed capacity.

[05:51] Alex: Great. Now quick ops notes — Jordan, can you confirm the primary contacts for each deal and the expected decision timelines?

[05:58] Jordan: Acme - decision target mid-March, contact is Maria Gonzalez (Head of Platform). Meridian - Q3 evaluation, contact is Ivan Petrov (Infra). NovaHealth - Q2 but needs compliance signoffs, contact is Dr. Kim (CTO).

[06:14] Samir: On the technical side I want to flag potential model compatibility issues; Acme tests a model family that uses a custom tokenizer. We'll want to validate tokenizer compatibility before the PoC. If there's a mismatch we can either run a conversion step or use a compatible model variant; that'll affect latency slightly.

[06:34] Ethan: Good to know — we'll include tokenizer samples in the Acme dossier.

[06:38] Priya: For the co-sell economics, we need a simple contract addendum that shows revenue share and responsibility matrix. Does Redwood do partner addenda or should we draft?

[06:48] Alex: We have a partner addendum template; I'll attach it. We typically outline responsibilities (billing, support handoff, SLAs) and the revenue split. Legal can adjust if Lumina wants different terms.

[06:59] Jordan: Anything else on the pipeline?

[07:02] Hannah: One more — competitors: Acme has evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI; they liked Anthropic's safety features but cost was high. How do we position Redwood versus those?

[07:13] Samir: We position on performance economics and operational controls — predictable cost with Dedicated, routing policies, caching and batch controls. Also our observability (Console) exposes per-route token costs so customers can tune. On safety features we have tooling for prompt filtering and evals tied to regression alerts.

[07:34] Jordan: Good. For the demo playbook, can you include a quick script for showing the Console cost breakdown? Our reps find that compelling.

[07:41] Maya: We'll include that and a short video clip.

[07:45] Alex: Alright let's summarize next steps before we run out of time. Jordan to share pipeline CSV and contacts by 2/9. Alex to send updated co-sell deck, partner addendum template, and pricing band by 2/8. Samir to run benchmark for Acme and share results by 2/15. Maya to push security pack and SOC2 artifacts to Jordan by end of day 2/6.

[08:10] Jordan: Sounds good. Also, can we plan a technical deep-dive for Meridian next Tuesday? I'd like Samir to join and bring the on-prem checklist.

[08:19] Samir: I can do Tuesday, I'll bring the checklist and a deployment runbook.

[08:24] Priya: Perfect, we'll schedule it and loop in Meridian infra.

[08:28] Alex: Cool — last thing, I'll log the joint activities in the CRM (CRM-94271-LUM) and tag the Acme opportunity for co-sell. Any final questions?

[08:38] Ethan: Quick clarification: for the Dedicated commit, do we have minimum capacity thresholds?

[08:44] Alex: We do have minimums depending on GPU class; I'll include the thresholds in the pricing band. Typically it's 2-4 reserved GPUs for initial commit for mid-market, but it varies.

[08:56] Jordan: Thanks everyone — this was helpful. We'll get the CSV over and look forward to the benchmarks.

[09:02] Alex: Thanks all, talk soon.

[09:05] (meeting ends)

Notes: Links referenced during call: co-sell deck (link shared in chat), security pack (to be shared by Maya), partner pipeline CSV (to be shared by Jordan). Transcript contains typical ASR errors (proper nouns sometimes garbled, K-V cash reference).
